3-way merge MANDATORY for all conflict resolution in pureclaw: use git show :1:<file> (base), :2:<file> (HEAD), :3:<file> (other branch); run diff base→HEAD and diff base→other SEPARATELY to see each side's intent against the shared parent. 2-way diff (just HEAD vs other) hides refactor intent: a function rename on one side + a call-site addition on the other looks ambiguous in 2-way but is unambiguous in 3-way. Always compile+test before staging — the compiler catches 3-way mistakes (missing record fields after a type refactor, broken imports after a module move). Authoritative procedure: docs/GIT_WORKFLOW.md (§Resolving Merge Conflicts). Mandatory rule stated in CLAUDE.md (Workflow Enforcement → Resolving Merge Conflicts MANDATORY 3-way). Lesson surfaced from PR #57 merge against main's Session/Tab Unification work — 2-way would have lost the SessionMeta runtime→kind refactor and the POST /api/sessions/new → 410 Gone migration.

AsyncCancelled discipline for tab loops (#51): catch SomeException EXCEPT AsyncCancelled. Pattern: catch with handler that does 'case fromException e :: Maybe AsyncCancelled of Just _ -> throwIO e; Nothing -> writeIORef _statusRef (Crashed ...)'. This lets bracket cleanup complete in close paths while still letting the loop transition to Crashed on synchronous failures. Applied in Tab.Ai/Harness/Backend factories (WU6/7/8). The Dispatcher.spawnTab swallows AsyncCancelled (WU5 reviewer concern #1) but the tab-loop level safelyRun re-raises it — bounded by the single-threaded dispatcher invariant.

Coverage staged-waiver discipline (post-WU6 of #57): a staged waiver in .coverage-thresholds.json is for HPC ACCOUNTING QUIRKS (per-derived-instance, per-let-binding, per-ToJSON-arm), NOT for missing tests. If a gap is closable by adding 2 fixtures and 2 assertion lines (as the original Activity.Types waiver was), close it — do not waive. The adversarial reviewer caught this exact pattern in WU6. Test before waiver. Waivers MUST list concrete behavioral DoDs in minimalChecks that are actually exercised — verify each by tracing to the test file. filledBy should name a concrete follow-up issue ID, not 'post-merge follow-up'.

Coverage stagedWaivers protocol (post-WU1 of #51): .coverage-thresholds.json supports a 'stagedWaivers.modules' map for modules whose executable bodies are deferred to later WUs by an approved plan. Each waiver requires stagedBy, filledBy (list of WUs), since, reason, minimalChecks (the concrete coverage-equivalent assertions that DO land in the staging WU). Orchestrator removes waiver when filledBy WUs land. Original 100% threshold was relaxed to 95% mid-#51 because chasing the last few percent on defensive-unreachable arms produced churn without bug-finding value. Pre-push hook only runs hlint+cabal test, not coverage.

Invariant: a session has EITHER a user custom-prompt.md (then _sm_agent must be null) XOR a named agent — never both. handleSetPrompt enforces it (clears _sm_agent, stores any provided name as _sm_description) and writes metadata before the prompt file so a decode failure can't leave the contradiction. Older on-disk sessions may still violate it; the frozen-prompt precedence (custom-prompt > agent) resolves them deterministically.

Cycle-break via .hs-boot files (WU3 #51): AgentEnv (Agent.Env) needs field types from Handles.Tab + Routing.Types; both those modules import Agent.SlashCommands; Agent.SlashCommands imports Agent.Env. Triangle cycle resolved with src/PureClaw/Handles/Tab.hs-boot and src/PureClaw/Routing/Types.hs-boot — minimal boot files exposing only the abstract types (TabHandle, TabIndex, TabRunner, RoutingConfig, OutputSource, ChannelEvent) that Agent.Env needs as field shapes. Agent.Env uses {-# SOURCE #-} imports. Sealed source files are byte-identical to HEAD. Cycle-killer also enforces: no module imports Tab.* except Routing.Dispatcher (verified).

Frontend AI-Harness/tmux sessions: spawn in createTab via _fe_startHarness seam (defer _fe_tabCount bump until success), persist tmux coords in _sm_kind HarnessSpec._h_backend=TbTmux TmuxConfig._tc_window=harnessKey, and handleSend must branch on _sm_kind BEFORE the provider/model 503 guard. Shared harnessRef IORef = _env_harnesses == _fe_harnesses.

A HarnessHandle records to its captured TranscriptHandle; for fresh frontend harness sessions pass mkNoOpTranscriptHandle so handleSend is the sole writer of the session transcript (no duplicate entries). Restart-discovered handles record to the CLI's own transcript (different file).

Lazy session creation is a frontend-only concern: 'New tab' and 'branch' set selectedId=null (compose mode) and defer the backend session to first send — handleComposerSend (App.tsx) POSTs /api/tabs/new then /api/sessions/{id}/send. createTab (Frontend/API.hs) persists SessionMeta+dir+transcript immediately when called AND bumps _fe_tabCount unconditionally with no decrement, so any fallible validation (e.g. branch resolution) must run BEFORE createTab or a failed request permanently consumes a tab slot.

MessageSource (PureClaw.Core.Types, pureclaw-dte) normalization is WRITE-TIME only: mkMessageSource strips control chars + bounds length (maxSourceLen=512) on the userId and every JSON String leaf in _ms_fields (incl. nested arrays/objects), and folds CkOther naming a known channel to the typed constructor (shadowing guard). The FromJSON decode trusts on-disk data (no re-normalization). Therefore ALL channel construction sites MUST use mkMessageSource, never the raw MessageSource record. _sm_source/_im_source/metadata.source are attacker-asserted provenance: never feed authz — routing keys on imUserId only.

mkTranscriptProvider's Text param is the MODEL NAME (populates _te_model), NOT a message source. When adding per-message provenance (pureclaw-dte), a SEPARATE 'Maybe MessageSource' param was added between the model Text and SomeProvider, written to _te_metadata under key 'source' on Request entries in BOTH complete AND completeStream (completeStream silently drops it otherwise). Response entries are never tagged.

Privacy boundary asymmetry in PureClaw frontend broadcast: transcript _te_metadata is broadcast-SAFE because TranscriptEntryInfo / toEntryInfo (Stream.hs) / toTranscriptEntryInfo (API.hs) project only id/timestamp/direction/payload/harness/model and DROP the metadata map. But SessionMeta is broadcast WHOLESALE via AkSessionCreated (Stream.hs ~178, 'session' .= meta). So any new PII field added to SessionMeta's ToJSON (e.g. _sm_source) is broadcast unless the publisher keeps it Nothing. See pureclaw-6nr.

pureclaw /bg command (#52, branch feat/bg-command): /bg <prompt> spawns a fresh background AI tab via dispatcher and pushes the result to the channel. Design: (1) background flag lives in AiTabState._ats_background (sourced from AiSpawnArgs._ai_background) NOT an AgentEnv field — it travels with the tab so it's immune to tmux index renumbering AND avoids touching 39 AgentEnv construction sites. (2) completion push fires in runOneTurn only when (_ats_background && not focusedNow), via emitBgCompletion -> (SrcDispatcher, BannerLine '[bg /N done] '<>body) which bypasses focus gating; only /bg tabs push, focused tabs stream live with no double-output. (3) handleBg deliberately omits writeIORef _env_focus (no focus steal). (4) bg-aware factory is injected by the dispatcher via SpawnIO so AutoSpawn stays decoupled from Tab.Ai. (5) bg tab name must be non-empty ('bg') — Parse.sanitizeTabName rejects '' as NameRedactedToEmpty so mkTabAi would return Left and spawn nothing. coverage enforcement is a manual agent check (cabal test --enable-coverage exits 0 regardless of %); Tab.Ai/Dispatcher/AutoSpawn are staged-waiver modules.

pureclaw build-warning caveat (discovered during /bg #52): -Wincomplete-patterns AND -Wmissing-fields are BOTH OFF (only -Wincomplete-uni-patterns + -Wpartial-fields are on, plus -Werror). Consequence: (1) adding a SlashCommand constructor compiles clean even if executeSlashCommand/dispatchSlash omit the arm — then crashes at runtime with Non-exhaustive patterns. executeSlashCommand has NO catch-all (must add arm); dispatchSlash HAS a '_ -> routeToFocused' catch-all (must add explicit arm or it silently mis-routes). (2) adding a record field compiles clean at construction sites that omit it — the strict field becomes bottom and throws when forced. So adding a SlashCommand constructor or a record field requires HAND-updating every match site / construction site; the build will NOT flag misses. e.g. AiSpawnArgs has 12 construction sites (1 prod parseArgsForKind + 11 test).

pureclaw production entry path (IMPORTANT correction, found via /bg #52): the production CLI 'runChat' (used by BOTH 'pureclaw tui' AND 'pureclaw gateway', CLI/Commands.hs:751) runs the LEGACY single-tab loop PureClaw.Agent.Loop.runAgentLoopWith — NOT PureClaw.Routing.Dispatcher.runDispatcher. The tabbed-chat dispatcher (runDispatcher) + ChannelOut writer are NOT wired to any production entry point yet (the WU10/WU11/WU12 refactor to make runAgentLoop a thin wrapper over runDispatcher was deferred). Consequence: any feature implemented ONLY in the dispatcher (e.g. /tab*, the dispatcher /bg handler) is UNREACHABLE in production; the legacy loop bridges /tab* via Routing.LegacyDispatch.dispatchLegacyTabCmd (emits via _ch_send directly, since no ChannelOut writer runs in the legacy path). For /bg this meant the dispatcher handler never ran — fixed by intercepting CmdBg in runAgentLoopWith and forking runBackgroundTurn (Loop.hs) which runs Tools.Delegate.runSubAgent in a fresh context and emits '[bg done] ...' directly via _ch_send. LESSON: before implementing a CLI-facing feature in the dispatcher, confirm which loop the production entry point actually runs.

pureclaw transcript/frontend visibility (found via /bg #52): EVERY conversation must have a frontend-visible transcript. A conversation is visible in the frontend UI iff it has an on-disk session dir under getSessionsDir (~/.pureclaw/sessions) with a NON-EMPTY transcript.jsonl — the frontend's GET /api/sessions/recent scans that dir (listSessions + hasTranscriptEntries) and the broker pushes live updates. To make any conversation visible: create a session via Session.mkSessionHandle (Just broker) logger sessionsDir meta (this creates session.json + transcript.jsonl AND wires the broadcasting transcript handle), and wrap the provider with PureClaw.Transcript.Provider.mkTranscriptProvider th (unModelId model) provider so each complete/completeStream records a request+response pair. Talking to a provider DIRECTLY (e.g. Tools.Delegate.runSubAgent with the raw provider) produces NO transcript and is invisible. runChat uses ONE sessionsDir for both the session and _fe_sessionsDir; getSessionsDir == getPureclawDir </> sessions == takeDirectory (_sh_dir foregroundSession). /bg now runs in its own fresh broker-wired session so it shows up as a separate conversation (Loop.runBackgroundSession/mkBackgroundSession).

Replay-with-since snapshot race-free algorithm (Frontend.Stream pattern): when reading transcript.jsonl for replay AND racing concurrent broker publishes, the safe pattern is: (1) atomically set replayMode TVar; while set, the writer thread BUFFERS incoming EntryRecorded for the focused sessionId in an IORef [TranscriptEntry] instead of forwarding; (2) read transcript.jsonl with try @SomeException, compute fileSlice (entries with id > since); (3) send fileSlice as entry events; (4) atomically drain the buffer with UUID-dedup against fileSlice ids, send remaining; (5) emit replay-end. Anomaly path: on any I/O error or unexpected state, emit replay-failed and let the client refetch via HTTP. This guarantees forward progress. KEY INVARIANT: every _te_id is a unique UUID allocated BEFORE _th_record is called (verified in Transcript.Combinator.withTranscript) — the dedup invariant the algorithm relies on.

Forking a session = copy the transcript prefix [0..K] verbatim + append. The fork inherits _sm_kind/_sm_model/_sm_agent from the source meta (keeps agent identity) and copies NO custom-prompt.md — the frozen prompt and last model already ride in the copied transcript. Harness (SkHarness) sessions are not forkable (plain-text exchanges, external-process state, no replayable history). Backend reads the prefix from the on-disk source (never client payloads); isValidSessionId guards traversal.

Session model and system prompt both 'ride in the transcript', frozen per session. doCompletion (Frontend/API.hs) reconstructs them from the most-recent recorded Request entry: system prompt via frozenSystemPrompt (frozen after turn 1; first turn computes custom-prompt.md > per-session agent rendered by composeAgentPromptWithBootstrap > global _fe_systemPrompt), model via lastRequestModel (request _sr_model > last _te_model > global _fe_model). The append-only transcript is the per-session source of truth; there is NO separate per-session model/prompt state. Editing an agent def or custom-prompt.md mid-session does NOT change an existing session.

STM-atomic publish protocol (PureClaw.Frontend.StreamBroker pattern): for pub/sub broker, the publish must atomically fan out to all subscriber queues in ONE atomically block, composing per-subscriber publishOne :: STM () (isFullTBQueue → readTBQueue (drop oldest) + writeTVar overflowFlag True (when full) → writeTBQueue ev). This linearizes the overflow protocol across all subscribers. Subscribers read the queue via STM orElse against the overflow TVar so they detect overflow in the same transaction. Cap-reached subscribe check must also be in the same STM transaction as the map mutation (no TOCTOU under concurrent subscribes). The cleaner is Map.delete on a Map (idempotent for double-cancel).

Tab factory triplicate pattern (#51): the three TabHandle factories (Tab.Ai.mkTabAi, Tab.Harness.mkTabHarness, Tab.Backend.mkTabBackend) all share: (1) per-tab state record with TBQueue for non-blocking _tabHandle_send (H4); (2) dual helper-thread design (drainer reads source → enqueues to _env_channelOutQ; writer drains send queue → backend) forked via _env_fork (never forkIO); (3) bracket-style status transitions (Idle→Active); (4) AsyncCancelled re-raise discipline; (5) sanitizeTabName for _tabHandle_name (H11); (6) shouldEmit from Routing.ChannelOut for D4 producer-side focus check. Non-AI factories return Left TabUnsupportedCommand on enqueueSlash.

Tabbed Chat (#51) post-PR follow-ups (deferred from WU9/WU10/WU12, all blocked on Agent.Loop refactor): 1) Agent.Loop.runAgentLoop should become a thin wrapper around Routing.Dispatcher.runDispatcher — currently the legacy single-tab loop coexists with the tabbed dispatcher. Blocked by Tab.Ai feature gap: missing model prefix emission, tool-call cycle, mkTranscriptProvider wrapping, _env_onFirstStreamDone callback, harness routing, no-provider/no-model help text. 2) H2 sig migration: 2-arg Handles.Tab.mk* stubs persist only to pin the H2 type-shape tests; migrate H2 to 3-arg Tab.{Ai,Harness,Backend}.mk* and delete stubs (clears Handles.Tab waiver). 3) _tabHandle_name in-place mutation for S10: requires TabHandle._tabHandle_name :: !TabName → IORef TabName cascade through Handles.Tab + 3 factories + H1 sig pin. 4) /N missing-index per-index spawn (currently spawns at lowest-free). Active waivers list these in filledBy.

Tabbed Chat tmux-style packing (post-#51 v1.5): tabs always occupy /0..K-1; gaps not allowed. /tab new takes no index (always allocates lowest free); /N on missing tab errors (no auto-spawn); /tab close N shifts all higher-indexed tabs down by 1 in _env_tabs, _env_runners, _ds_spawnArgs, _ds_pendingRetry. Focus rule: focus==closedN → Nothing; focus>closedN → decrement; focus<closedN → unchanged. K3 first-run UX preserved (empty registry + Default text → auto-spawn at slot 0). TabHandle._tabHandle_index is advisory after renumber (creation slot, not current); registry key is canonical. ADT change: TabNewCmd dropped its Int arg → TabNewCmd !(Maybe TabKindArg) !(Maybe Text). docs/tabbed-chat.md is stale on A-series and L6 — needs follow-up paperwork.

WebSocket Origin allowlist discipline (PureClaw normalizeOrigin pattern): WS upgrades are NOT protected by browser CORS the way XHR is. A drive-by malicious local page can open a WS without a preflight. Mandatory: validate Origin header with EXACT-MATCH against an allowlist, after a normalizeOrigin pass (lowercase scheme + host, strip trailing /, no Unicode normalization, no wildcards). Missing Origin → deny. Empty allowlist → deny all. Substring attacks like 'http://localhost.evil.com:8080' must be rejected — a naive prefix check would admit them. Per-origin subscriber cap (StreamGuard) keys the TVar (Map Text Int) by the NORMALIZED origin, not the raw header, otherwise a peer alternating case can get 2x slots.

WS keepalive: Warp setTimeout does NOT apply to hijacked WebSocket sockets (wai-websockets responseRaw hijacks the socket out of Warp's connection table). For WS, use Network.WebSockets.withPingThread with a paired pong timeout (PureClaw uses 25s/10s = 35s forced-disconnect budget). Discovered during WU3 of #57; documented in docs/SECURITY_PRACTICES.md §9.1.1 + SERVICE-INVENTORY.md established patterns. Without this, the 'setMaxTotalConnections + setTimeout' protection that works for HTTP routes is a no-op on WS, exposing slow-loris on persistent connections.

WU3 split-fallback pattern (post-#57): for large WUs with mixed production-and-test scope (24 DoDs, ~600+500 LoC), pre-commit a 'split fallback' in the plan: WU3a = production code + unit tests; WU3b = integration tests + golden fixtures. The coder triggers the fallback when scope clearly overruns. This gives the orchestrator a clean escalation path without scope creep. The split also exposes spec divergences that purely-unit-test coverage hides: WU3a's adversarial review found D40 (replay-aborted on mid-replay focus switch) was structurally unreachable from the single-threaded reader thread because startReplay runs synchronously — a fix that requires Async, filed as pureclaw-jdg.10. Without integration tests in WU3b, the spec divergence would have shipped invisibly.
